newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Jan 28.

text.p: - Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters
-- ROLLS-ROYCE ADMITS ENGINE FAILURES

British engineering group Rolls-Royce Plc has admitted to problems with a version of one of its aircraft engines, leading to some in-flight engine shutdowns. The problem engines are in use on Boeing 747s and 767s, the most widely used long-haul aircraft, although Rolls-Royce has emphasised that none of the engine shutdowns has posed any danger to passengers.
-- ELECTROLUX CHIEF TO TAKE OVER AS GYLL LEAVES VOLVO

Swedish automotive giant Volvo has announced a successor to Soren Gyll after his shock resignation as chief executive. Leif Johansson, chief executive of Electrolux, will take control in April. With Volvo currently limited to a narrow model range and production of just 350,000 units last year, it remains a potential target for a merger or takeover despite the failure of a merger with Renault in 1993 due to shareholder pressure. Johansson has hinted that an expansion of the product range, in particular through a new, smaller car, is one option to be considered by the company.
-- MIDLANDS EMPLOYERS HIT BY SKILLS SHORTAGE

Employers in the West Midlands have said that a shortage of skilled workers is giving them their worst recruitment difficulties in over six years. The region has the least qualified workforce in Britain, as measured by national vocational qualifications. Employers in the manufacturing and services industries have said that recruitment of skilled and semi-skilled labour in the region has become substantially harder in the past three months, and have pointed to a number of reasons including a poorly-motivated workforce.
-- CLARKE EXPECTED TO STAND FIRM ON RATES DESPITE GROWTH

Chancellor Kenneth Clarke is expected to resist pressure to raise interest rates despite figures from the Office of National Statistics published on Monday, which show that economic growth accelerated to its fastest rate for two years at the end of 1996. The figures show that gross domestic product grew by a seasonally adjusted 0.8 percent between the third and fourth quarters of 1996, an increase in line with City expectations and which should have little influence on the future direction of interest rate changes.
-- HOUSE OF FRASER TO CUT 1,000 JOBS IN SHAKE-UP

Department store chain House of Fraser is to sell or close three stores and cut 1,000 jobs as part of a restructuring which is expected to provide initial savings of 10 million stg a year. The announcement was made in a surprisingly upbeat Christmas trading statement, which revealed that comparable sales for the group were up 6.1 percent for the 26 weeks to January 25.
-- INGERSOLL-RAND IN 230 MILLION STG BID FOR NEWMAN TONKS

U.S. industrial equipment group Ingersoll-Rand is set to acquire British architectural hardware company Newman Tonks in a 230 million stg agreed takeover. The cash offer trumps the hostile 189 million stg bid from diversified British engineering company FKI. Newman Tonks is recommending shareholders accept the Ingersoll-Rand offer, which the U.S. group said signalled an acceleration of its European expansion strategy.
-- GULF BID TOO LOW, SAYS CLYDE

Clyde Petroleum, the British oil independent which is currently the subject of a 432 million stg hostile takeover bid from Gulf Canada Resources, is to publish its final defence document on Tuesday. Clyde is expected to claim that it is worth around 130p a share, or 103 million stg more than the
Gulf offer.
-- GENERAL MOTORS TO BUY BACK $2.5 BILLION SHARES

General Motors, the largest automotive manufacturer in the United States, is set to buy back $2.5 billion (1.49 billion stg) of its shares, and to raise its dividend by 25 percent. The move marks a turnaround for GM, which five years ago was forced to turn to the equity markets for $2 billion. However, the scale of the planned buy back is more modest that Wall Street analysts had hoped, and is being seen as an indication that GM is still some way from the completion of its restructuring plans.
-- HANSON'S FOUR-WAY DEMERGER ENTERS FINAL PHASE

Former British conglomerate Hanson is set to mark the final phase of its four-way demerger with the publication of listing particulars for its coal and power arm Energy Group, and trading figures from the rump building materials operations. The document for Energy Group -- which comprises British utility Eastern Group as well as U.S. coal producer Peabody -- is expected to show a more global strategy for the group, with directors looking to acquisition and investment opportunities in North America and southeast Asia.
